sections.heading: Economic issues from bifurcation & central assistance

blocks.text: The **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** created several **economic issues** for residuary Andhra Pradesh — a **revenue deficit, loss of the capital, and unfulfilled promises** — for which the Act and subsequent commitments provided for **central assistance and special provisions**.

rows: Act provides central funding for the **resource-gap/revenue deficit** for the first year (& beyond).
Central support pledged for building a **new capital (Amaravati)**.
**Special development package** for backward districts (Rayalaseema & North Coastal AP).
New central institutions (IIT, IIM, NIT, central university, AIIMS, etc.) promised.
Debate over **Special Category Status vs Special Assistance/Package**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: bifurcation economics & central assistance

items: **Fiscal shock**: loss of Hyderabad's revenue left AP with a **resource gap & revenue deficit**; the AP Reorganisation Act promised central support — a **special development package**, backward-region grants (Rayalaseema & North Coastal Andhra), tax incentives, and institutions.

**Central assistance actually given**: revenue-deficit grant (partial), a **special package** (later, in lieu of Special Category Status), assistance for the new capital & Polavaram (national project, largely centrally funded), backward-districts funds.
**Promised institutions**: national institutions for AP (IIT-Tirupati, IIM-Visakhapatnam, IISER, Central University, NIT, IIIT, AIIMS-Mangalagiri, tribal & petroleum universities) — most established.
**Ongoing disputes**: quantum of assistance, pending division of Schedule IX/X institutions, power dues, and the **Special Category Status** question.
AP Reorganisation Act 2014 promised: revenue-deficit funding, new capital support, backward-area package, central institutions.
The Special Category Status debate stems from these commitments.

sections.heading: Specific issues — Vizag railway zone, Kadapa steel, Dugarajapatnam airport, corridors

blocks.text: The demand for **Special Category Status (SCS)** for Andhra Pradesh became the central post-bifurcation political-economic controversy — pitting the state's claim (based on assurances at bifurcation) against the Centre's offer of a **Special Assistance Package** instead.

rows: Historically granted to states with special disadvantages; gives higher central funding (90:10 grants).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Special Category Status controversy

items: **Special Category Status (SCS)**: a classification (originated with the **5th Finance Commission/Gadgil formula, 1969**) for states with hilly terrain, low density, strategic borders, tribal population, economic backwardness — giving higher central grants (90:10 funding), tax concessions. Original SCS states = NE + hilly (11).
**AP's demand**: the then-PM's assurance on the floor of the Rajya Sabha (Feb 2014) during bifurcation raised expectations of SCS for AP.

**Centre's stand**: the **14th Finance Commission** effectively **discontinued the SCS category** (folding it into higher tax devolution, 42%); the Centre offered a **Special Package/assistance in lieu of SCS** — a long-running political dispute in AP.
**Significance**: SCS is a live prelims/interview issue on **fiscal federalism, promises vs delivery, and centre-state relations**.
SCS demand rooted in 2014 bifurcation assurances; 14th FC ended the SCS category.
Centre offered Special Assistance Package instead — the core controversy.
